title: Lesson 7
paragraph: 判断と理解の落とし穴

words.meaning: to decide that something is true before considering enough information
words.japaneseMeaning: 十分に考えず結論を出す
words.example: Don't jump to conclusions before you hear her explanation.

sentencePractice.prompt: We have not checked the facts. Do not ____ by deciding already that one employee is to blame.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: Assigning blame before checking evidence is premature. Keeping an open mind or reserving judgment avoids that early conclusion.

words.meaning: to fail to understand the main idea or purpose
words.example: If you focus only on the price, you miss the point of the proposal.
meaningDistractors: hit the nail on the head

words.word: get the wrong end of the stick
words.japaneseMeaning: 話の意味を取り違える
words.example: You may get the wrong end of the stick if you read only the last message.
words.usageNote: 主に会話で使う、相手の意図を取り違える表現です。

words.meaning: to work out what has happened by connecting pieces of information
words.japaneseMeaning: 手掛かりを結び付けて事情を察する
words.example: I saw the packed boxes and put two and two together: they were moving.

words.meaning: a practical guide based on experience rather than an exact calculation
words.japaneseMeaning: 経験に基づく大まかな目安
words.example: As a rule of thumb, leave extra time when you travel during rush hour.

words.word: take something with a pinch of salt
words.meaning: to avoid fully believing a statement because it may not be accurate
words.japaneseMeaning: 話をうのみにせず受け止める
words.example: I take those online rumors with a pinch of salt until a reliable source confirms them.

exampleGap.prompt: I ____ until a reliable source confirms them.
exampleGap.answer: take those online rumors with a pinch of salt

meaningDistractors: give someone the benefit of the doubt
let the cat out of the bag
words.usageNote: アメリカ英語では with a grain of salt も一般的です。something は the claim などに置き換えます。

words.meaning: to avoid choosing between opposing sides or opinions
words.japaneseMeaning: どちらにも決めず態度を保留する
words.example: The committee needs a decision; we cannot sit on the fence forever.

sentencePractice.prompt: Asked to support either side, I refuse to choose and continue to ____.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: Refusing to choose defines remaining undecided between sides. Taking a side or deciding is the opposite response.

words.meaning: to notice other people's feelings so you can respond appropriately
words.japaneseMeaning: その場の人々の気持ちや空気を読む
words.example: A good host can read the room and change the topic when guests feel uncomfortable.

words.meaning: to remain willing to consider ideas you have not yet accepted
words.japaneseMeaning: 先入観を持たず検討する姿勢を保つ
words.example: Keep an open mind when you listen to the other group's proposal.

words.word: give someone the benefit of the doubt
words.meaning: to judge someone fairly by accepting that they may be honest when the facts are uncertain
words.japaneseMeaning: 証拠がはっきりしないとき相手を善意に解釈する
words.example: I try to give someone the benefit of the doubt before assuming that a mistake was deliberate.
